To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

metallothionein-null mice have reduced bactericidal activity against Staphylococcal aureus, reduced nitric oxide (a bactericidal agent) production, and decreased expression of inducibe nitric oxide synthase, the enzyme that produces nitric oxide.
metallothionein is involved in the bactericidial activity and nitric-oxide production of macrophages.

MT-null Mvarphis have reduced bactericidal activity against S. aureus, reduced NO production in response to L-arginine, reduced NO production and iNOS activity, and reduced conversion of [(14C)-l-arginine in response to TN-alpha and LPS stimulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of MT in the bactericidial activity and the mechanism of NO production by Mvarphi.
the bactericidal activity in macrophages from MT-null mice.
the role of metallothionein in the immune response of macrophages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduced bactericidal activity in MT-null Mphi is mainly due to reduced NO production, which is due to the reduced activity of iNOs.
the bactericidal activity in MT-deficient macrophage cells is decreased due to the reduced production of nitric oxide.
MT-null Mvarphis are less able to kill S. aureus and produce NO, which is an important factor for the bactericidal activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduced NO production in MT-null Mphi is due mainly not to reduced expression of iNOS or arginase but to reduced activity of the iNOS enzyme itself.
MT-null mice have a reduced ability to fight against bacterial infection, and this may be related to the reduced production of TNF-alpha in the MT-null mice.
metallothionein is an important factor to maintain the bactericidal activity against Staphylococci and to regulate the NO production in the macrophages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MT-null Mvarphis are defective in their ability to produce NO in response to LIP stimulation.
the reduced bactericidal activity in MT-null Mvaphi is mainly caused by reduced NO production.
metallothionein plays important roles in the activation of macrophage bactericidal activity by enhancing nitric oxide production.
